drivers.driver: The earnings yield of equities significantly exceeds the long government bond yield by nearly 5 percentage points, offering superior long-term owner returns [D04].
Institutional sentiment is notably pessimistic, with private pension allocations to equities at a record low of 9%, signaling widespread fear [D03, D06].
Broad market valuations remain depressed, with the Dow trading below book value, providing a substantial margin of safety for the patient investor [D02, D04].

final.memo:
Charlie and I find that the current environment offers a compelling opportunity to purchase pieces of wonderful businesses at prices that provide a significant margin of safety [D04, D06]. When the earnings yield of the market exceeds the long bond yield by such a wide margin, we need not concern ourselves with the near-term path of the market index, which remains a distraction from the fundamental business economics [D01, D04].

While others are fearful, as evidenced by the extremely low allocation of pension funds into equities, we see no reason to hold excess cash when established franchises are available at prices below their intrinsic value [D03, D04]. We remain focused on finding businesses with durable competitive advantages and the ability to maintain pricing power in an inflationary environment, rather than speculating on turnarounds or new industries [D01, D06]. Our holding period remains indefinite, and we are content to act decisively when the arithmetic of value so clearly favors ownership over the duration risk of bonds [D01, D04].
